productsAndServices.name: Factorized Power Architecture (FPA™) — PRM™ regulators and VTM™ current multipliers for 48 V point-of-load
productsAndServices.description: Vicor's proprietary distribution architecture, per its 10-K: an implementation 'for delivering 48V DC from a server backplane to a 1.0V microprocessor would consist of three modules: a PRM™ (Pre-Regulator Module) regulator, a VTM™ (Voltage Transformation Module) current multiplier, and a proprietary communications controller', with 'a regulated voltage approaching 48V … bussed across the circuit to the transformation module, which performs what we refer to as current multiplication, adjacent to the load'. The PRM is a zero-voltage-switching buck-boost regulator ('99.3% peak being achieved with the latest PRMs' per the FPA white paper); the VTM is a fixed-ratio Sine Amplitude Converter™ (SAC™) — 'a proprietary multi-megahertz ZCS/ZVS' topology — that divides the regulated 48 V bus by a K factor (1/40 to 1) and multiplies the current by the same factor at the point of load, responding 'to load changes regardless of magnitude in less than one microsecond' (typically 400 ns). Sold as discrete Full-Chip, Half-Chip and SM-ChiP modules and as the building block of the Power-on-Package and VPD lines below.
highlights: Regulation and transformation are separated: the PRM regulates upstream at ~48 V where the current is small, and the VTM multiplies current next to the load — per the FPA white paper, 'a current gain of 1:48 or higher to provide higher efficiency, smaller size, faster response and scalability to 1000A and beyond'

Catalogue VTMs run from 26–55 V in to 0.7–1.4 V out at 130 A (VTM48EF012T130C01, K = 1/40, '>94%' efficiency, '443 A/in³') up to 26–55 V out at 6.3 A; PRMs from 400 W to 800 W (PRM2313S60E54H0T00, 38–60 V in, 30–54 V out) per the family overview (Rev 3.1, 02/2024)

Because the VTM's K factor scales capacitance by K², 'the capacitance value can be reduced by a factor of 1600' at the point of load versus a 48 V-side placement (VTM48EF012 datasheet) — the mechanism behind Vicor's small-footprint claims
Family overview claims 'Regulation 0.2% (Remote Sense)', 'Power density up to 2,040W/in3', 'Low profile: 0.265in' and VTM 'isolation to 2,250VDC' — quoted values, not independently tested
The same PRM + VTM chain is the 48 V-side half of every Vicor 800 V and 400 V rack chain (the BCM6135 datasheet's typical-application diagram shows 'BCM6135… with PRM™ + VTM™ and MCD + MCM™')
productsAndServices.positioning: Against the multiphase-buck voltage regulators that Monolithic Power Systems, Infineon, Renesas, Analog Devices and Texas Instruments sell for 48 V and 12 V point-of-load (all of them, and not Vicor, on NVIDIA's published 800 VDC silicon partner lists of May 2025, October 2025 and March 2026), Vicor's argument is architectural rather than per-part: its FPA article claims '48V FPA dissipates 35W versus 2.2kW for 6V IBA' for the same processor. SemiAnalysis's 2023 history (independent) records Vicor 'designed out' of NVIDIA's H100 and 'replaced by Monolithic Power Systems', after V100/A100, Google TPU, AMD MI300, Tesla, Intel and Cerebras wins — so the position is contested socket by socket, and Vicor's 2026 ITC complaint names MPS's MPC12109 module and AMD MI3XX boards as the accused products.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct sales and distribution (Mouser, Macnica and Marubun in Japan, ASTI, per Vicor's event releases) for catalogue modules; design-in engagements with AI OEMs and hyperscalers for custom Power-on-Package and VPD; and, since 2025, patent licences that let OEMs and contract manufacturers source FPA-covered designs from others (see the IP licensing line)
targetSegments: AI accelerator, GPU, TPU and wafer-scale processor boards
high-performance computing and automatic test equipment (ATE)
48 V automotive zonal and 48 V industrial systems
productsAndServices.roadmap: '5th generation ChiPs and 2nd Generation VPD' (Q3 2025 release) with a Q1 2026 production launch for the lead customer stated on the Q3 2025 call (trade-press transcript); an 'alternate source of high current density 2nd Gen VPD modules' for licensed OEMs and hyperscalers under exploration (Q4 2025 release); a second ChiP fab 'for high current density 2nd Gen VPD ChiPs' in site selection (Q2 2026 release). Vicor states it is 'feeding IVRs with a current multiplier' as an incremental opportunity (Q2 2026 release).

productsAndServices.name: Power-on-Package and Vertical Power Delivery — MCM/MCD ChiP-sets, GCM/GTM current multipliers, Gen 5 ChiPs and 2nd-Gen VPD
productsAndServices.description: The last-centimetre line. Per the 10-K, Vicor's 'most popular Power-on-Package solution, consists of one MCD (Modular Current Driver) unit, providing high-bandwidth, low-noise regulation, and two MCM (Modular Current Multiplier) units, providing high performance current multiplication', delivering 'unprecedented current levels to GPUs and AI ASICs, in part due to the placement of the MCMs directly on the substrate onto which the processor is mounted, thereby minimizing distribution losses'. The lateral form (LPD) flanks the processor with current multipliers on the board; the vertical form (VPD) stacks 'current multipliers and bypass capacitors … on each other to form an integrated power module' mounted directly under the processor, with a custom GCM (Geared Current Multiplier) that maps the multiplier pinout to the processor's BGA. Company-stated headline figures: current density 'greater than 3.0A/mm²' with current gain 'greater than 40', modules '1.5mm thin' with 'a thermal resistance of 0.3°C/W'; the FPA article gives '5A/mm2 TDC (continuous), 10A/mm2 peak', 'up to 60x' gain, '600A' continuous per module and a transient response of 'Less than 100nsec'. The 2020 MCD4609 + 2× MCM4609 ChiP-set supplies 'up to 650A continuous and 1200A peak' from 48 V. The successor — '5th generation ChiPs and 2nd Generation VPD' — exists on first-party channels only as CEO statements in results releases; no product page, part number or datasheet was found.
highlights: Vicor's own worked examples: an LPD design at ~800 A and 0.8 V with a 70 µΩ PDN using '2.8-mm-tall current multipliers'; a VPD design at 1,200 A with a 10 µΩ PDN (~14.4 W of PDN loss); VPD claimed to cut PDN losses 'by up to 50%' and to save 'about 100W per accelerator module versus traditional TLVR lateral power delivery' (company articles)

Q3 2025 call (trade-press transcript): Gen 5 VPD for the lead customer 'met target specifications' and was 'progressing to a Q1 2026 production launch', at 'up to five amperes per square millimeter peak current density' in a '1.5 millimeter thin' package; Q1 2026 call: 3 A/mm² baseline and 40× multiplication; Q2 2026 call: '>4 A/mm²' targeted around year-end, with sampling of the improved 2nd-gen part to Cerebras in Q1 2027 per Investing.com — the customer is unconfirmed by Vicor, which declined to name it on the call

The 2nd-Gen VPD IP is licensed as well as sold: the May 2026 OEM licence is 'all-inclusive' across 'Factorized Power (FPA) and Vertical Power Delivery (VPD)', and Vicor says it is 'exploring opportunities to expand total capacity by enabling an alternate source of high current density 2nd Gen VPD modules' (Q4 2025 release)

Independent history (SemiAnalysis, Aug 2023): Power-on-Package won V100, A100, Google TPU, AMD MI300, Tesla, Intel Gaudi3/PVC and Cerebras WSE2 sockets and was 'designed out' of H100 for MPS — the pattern is high-current design wins that are re-competed every generation

Craig-Hallum (Oct 2025) caveat, independent: the newest VPD product 'lacks field experience'; PhotonCap (Apr 2026): Vicor's 'performance claims lack independent third-party verification or disclosed competitor benchmarks'
productsAndServices.positioning: Vicor claims VPD is the only architecture that can serve the next generation of TPUs, GPUs and wafer-scale engines — 'AI OEMs and Hyper-scalers are at a loss dealing with the current density and PDN limitations of 1st Gen. VPD systems' (Q2 2026 release) — and its VP of strategic marketing argued in Power Electronics News (July 2026) that VPD is 'effectively unavoidable' by about 2029 while in-package integrated voltage regulators offer 'no opportunity for rework'. The native VPD competitors trade press names are Infineon's quad-phase modules, MPS's Z-axis Power Delivery, Renesas power towers and, after Analog Devices' $1.5 billion purchase of Empower Semiconductor (Zacks), ADI's in-package regulators; Vicor's counter-position is to supply 'a building block that is critical to deployment of IVRs' — a current multiplier feeding the on-package regulator — which it says two companies have approached it for (Q2 2026 call).
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct design-in with the processor OEM or hyperscaler (custom GCM/GTM pinouts per processor) and the accelerator-board contract manufacturer; the module is built in Vicor's Andover ChiP fab; licensing offers a second path for OEMs that want an alternate source
targetSegments: AI training accelerators, TPUs and wafer-scale engines
GPU and ASIC accelerator boards for OEMs and hyperscalers
high-current ATE and HPC boards
productsAndServices.roadmap: Q1 2026 production launch of Gen 5 VPD for the lead customer (Q3 2025 call); a second '3Di line' in Fab 1 in 3Q–4Q 2026 (Zacks); improved 2nd-gen VPD demo systems in 2026 with volume ramps 'late third quarter, fourth quarter' of 2027 (Phil Davies, Q2 2026 call, trade-press transcript); a second ChiP fab dedicated to 'high current density 2nd Gen VPD ChiPs' (Q2 2026 release).

productsAndServices.name: BCM® isolated fixed-ratio bus converters — 800 V and 400 V to 48 V, 48 V to 12 V (ChiP, SM-ChiP, CM-ChiP and VIA packages)
productsAndServices.category: High-voltage DC-DC bus conversion (800 VDC / 400 VDC racks, automotive, defense)
productsAndServices.description: Per the BCM family overview, 'Essentially a very small high-frequency DC-DC transformer, the BCM steps down its input voltage by a range of ratios and provides galvanic isolation … With peak efficiencies of up to 98% and power densities of up to 2,870W/in³', in three input tiers — 'Ultra-high voltage: 400 – 800V input', 'High voltage: 200 – 410V input (meets ETSI requirements)' and 'Low voltage: 36 – 60V input' — and 'When BCMs operate in reverse, they provide an efficient step-up conversion.' The family page lists inputs from 36 V to 800 V, outputs of 2.4–55 V, currents to 150 A and efficiency 'Up to 98%'; the HV-to-48V page states 'As small as 22.0 x 16.5 x 6.7mm'. The 800 V data-center part is the BCM4414 (500–800 V in, K = 1/16, 31.3–50 V out, 35 A, VIA package with PMBus); the 380/384 V part is the BCM6135CD1E5165 (260–410 V in, K = 1/8, 65 A, '3.4kW/in³', '97.9% peak efficiency', '4,242VDC isolation') — whose current datasheet is stamped 'Not Recommended for New Designs'; the automotive-grade BCM6135 800 V-to-48 V (520–920 V in, 32.5–57.5 V out, up to 80 A, 2.5 kW, 97.3% peak) is listed as Available and won three industry awards in early 2026.
highlights: Vicor's own 800 V argument, from 'Disaggregating Power in Data Centers': a 140 kW rack draws '350A at 400VDC and 175A at 800VDC'; '500MCM gauge copper cable for 400VDC distribution costs about $14 per foot, and 3/0AWG copper cable for 800VDC distribution costs about $5 per foot'; and a 1:8 fixed-ratio stage at 140 kW 'yields 2,800A at 50VDC'
The K factor scales bulk capacitance as K²: the 384 V BCM6135 datasheet describes 'enabling bulk capacitance across the 48V bus to be scaled down by a factor of 1/64 across the 384V bus'

'Inherently bidirectional' with 'Transient response times of eight million amps per second' and 'up to 65A (over 3000W) of power continuously' for the BCM6135 (company article on 800 V to 48 V SELV conversion); the company's own pages give the automotive module's weight as both 58 g and 65 g — no datasheet located for that variant

The foundational-patent claim behind the 2025 exclusion order covers '800V, 48V, and 12V bus converters' (Oct 2025 licensing release); the ITC's 2025 determination found Delta's power converter modules infringed the '761 patent while its redesigned products did not infringe the '481 and '950 patents
productsAndServices.positioning: Against the 800 V → 50 V DC-DC shelves that Delta (1RU 90 kW, 98.5%), LITEON and Megmeet build for NVIDIA's 800 VDC racks, Vicor sells the converter module rather than the shelf — the BCM is a component a shelf or a tray designer places, and Vicor's rack chain puts it at the tray ('compact 400 to 48V conversion within the rack … can increase the number of processors in each rack by fourfold', HV-to-48V page). Vicor is absent from NVIDIA's published 800 VDC component and silicon partner lists; its route into those racks is the module socket at the contract manufacturer and the patent licence over the bus-converter designs those shelves use.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Catalogue sales through distribution and direct; automotive-grade variants through Tier-1 and OEM design-ins (Hongfa active suspension customer story; co-developed 400–800 V and 400–12 V automotive units shown at AEE Nagoya, June 2026); MIL-COTS variants for defense primes; and the licence route for OEMs and contract manufacturers
targetSegments: 800 VDC and 380/400 VDC data-center racks and power shelves
800 V-to-48 V automotive zonal architectures and 48 V mild-hybrid systems
aerospace and defense 270 V / 800 V platforms, ATE
productsAndServices.roadmap: A 400 V/48 V BCM6135 (260–410 V in, up to 65 A, 2.5 kW, 97.9%) listed as Upcoming; an NBM9280 800 V/400 V non-isolated converter (200–460 V ↔ 400–920 V, 37 kW, 99.0% peak, 92 × 80 × 7.4 mm) listed as Upcoming on the automotive listing; the second ITC investigation (337-TA-1484) over a series-connected bus-converter patent runs to a target date of September 20, 2027.

productsAndServices.name: NBM™ non-isolated bidirectional bus converters — 48 V ↔ 12 V
productsAndServices.category: 48 V to 12 V bus conversion (servers, HPC, automotive 48/12 V)
productsAndServices.description: Fixed-ratio, non-isolated Sine Amplitude Converters that bridge the 48 V and 12 V worlds in either direction — 'Bidirectional power converters', 'Input Voltage: 36 – 60V', 'Output Voltage: 7.2 – 15.3V', 'Power: Up to 2400W', 'Efficiency: Over 98%' per the family page, with 'high power density of up to 3,600W/in3'. The NBM2317 (2317 SM-ChiP, 22.80 × 17.30 × 5.20 mm) delivers 65 A or 80 A at K = 1/4 from 40–60 V; the NBM6123 (61.00 × 25.14 × 7.21 mm) delivers 160–170 A at K = 1/3 or 1/5. The NBM2317S60D1580 datasheet (Rev 1.4, 01/2025) states '97.9% peak efficiency', 'Up to 8kW/in3 power density', '1000W / Up to 1.5kW, 2ms peak power capability', '80A continuous / 120A transient' step-down and '20A continuous / 30A transient' step-up, and a weight of 8.67 g. The Computing page describes NBMs as 'high-efficiency DC transformers' with 'bidirectional capability'. Vicor's February 2026 release says the ITC 'has recently instituted a second investigation into illegal importation of power modules and computing systems infringing Vicor's IP to Non-isolated Bus Converters ("NBMs")'.
highlights: The bridge product for 48 V racks that still carry 12 V loads — 'With a high-side to low-side K factor of 1/4, that capacitance value can be reduced by a factor of 16x' (NBM2317 datasheet)
Bidirectional start-up and steady-state operation lets the same module take a 12 V legacy bus up to 48 V — the 48 V-to-12 V and 12 V-to-48 V use cases share one part

The 2026 ITC complaint (337-TA-1484) on the '087 patent, 'Power Distribution Architecture with Series-Connected Bus Converter', names MPS's MPC12109-F-54-1000-0380 module and Wistron/Quanta servers with AMD MI3XX GPU boards as the accused products (trade-press summary of the public complaint)
productsAndServices.positioning: Vicor's non-isolated bus converter competes with the 48 V-to-12 V intermediate-bus converters from MPS, Infineon, Delta and the power-shelf vendors' own DC-DC bricks (LITEON's 2.5 kW 50 V → 12 V brick, Delta's DC-DC modules); the 2026 ITC action is the company's attempt to assert its bus-converter patents over that class of part as well.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Catalogue and distribution; automotive-grade variants (NBM2317 'TMR') for 48/12 V vehicle systems; licence route for infringing designs after any exclusion order
targetSegments: 48 V servers and accelerator boards with 12 V legacy rails
48/12 V automotive and industrial systems
HPC and ATE
productsAndServices.roadmap: NBM9280 800 V/400 V non-isolated 37 kW converter listed as Upcoming (automotive listing); the 337-TA-1484 final initial determination is due May 20, 2027 with a target date of September 20, 2027.

productsAndServices.name: DCM™ regulated DC-DC converters — isolated wide-input DCMs and the non-isolated 48 V-to-12 V DCM3717/DCM3735
productsAndServices.category: Regulated DC-DC conversion (48 V systems, industrial, MIL-COTS)
productsAndServices.description: The regulated half of the catalogue. The isolated DCM is 'an isolated, regulated DC-DC converter, operating from an unregulated, wide range input to generate an isolated output' on a ZVS topology, with inputs from 9 V to 420 V (family page tiers 9–36 V through 36–75 V; the HV-to-48V page states 'Input: 9 – 420V', 'Peak efficiency: 96%'), outputs of 3.3 V to 48 V and 35–320 W in 2322 and 3623 ChiP and 3414 VIA packages; MIL-COTS DCMs run to 1,300 W from 28, 30 and 270 V inputs. The March 2025 launch added the non-isolated 48 V-to-12 V DCM3717 and DCM3735 — 'regulated DC-DC converter modules that operate from a semi-regulated 40 – 60V input to generate a regulated point-of-load output with a voltage range of 10.0 – 12.5V', built as 'the Vicor patented zero-voltage switching (ZVS) buck-boost regulator stage followed by the Sine Amplitude Converter (SAC™)' at '>1MHz switching frequency', 750 W to 2 kW 'with an industry-leading power density of 5kW/in³', PMBus telemetry and arrays of up to four units. No 800 V-input regulated DCM exists on first-party channels — Vicor's regulated inputs top out at 420 V and 800 V is handled by fixed-ratio BCMs.
highlights: DCM3717: 54 V (40–60 V) in, 12.2 V (10–12.5 V) out, 750 W or 1,000 W, 96.5%, 36.7 × 17.3 × 5.2 mm SM-ChiP, released; DCM3735: 2,000 W, 96.4%, 36.7 × 35.4 × 5.2 mm, listed 'Coming Soon' in the July 2025 family overview and shown at Automotive Engineering Exposition Yokohama in May 2025
Automotive-grade DCM3735 (35–58 V → 8–16 V, 2 kW, up to 160 A, 96.5%) and PRM3735 (31–58 V → 36–54 V, 2.5 kW, up to 52 A, 99.2%) were introduced with the automotive BCM6135 in October 2024

Where a regulated output is needed the DCM is the whole converter; where the chain is factorized it is the PRM that regulates and a fixed-ratio stage that transforms — the two philosophies coexist in the catalogue
productsAndServices.positioning: Competes with the isolated brick and quarter-brick converters from Flex Power Modules, Advanced Energy, Delta and Murata, and with regulated 48 V-to-12 V modules from MPS and Infineon; Vicor's claim is density (5 kW/in³) and the ZVS efficiency of its regulator stage rather than price.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Catalogue and distribution; automotive Tier-1 design-ins; MIL-COTS through defense primes
targetSegments: 48 V industrial and telecom systems
48/12 V automotive zonal architectures
MIL-COTS avionics, vetronics and naval systems (28 V, 270 V)
productsAndServices.roadmap: DCM3735 volume release ('Coming Soon', July 2025 overview); automotive-grade DCM3735 'also available' per the same overview.

productsAndServices.name: PFM™ AC-DC front ends and ZVS buck regulators
productsAndServices.category: AC input and low-voltage point-of-load (industrial, telecom, defense)
productsAndServices.description: Two smaller lines that complete a Vicor-only chain from the wall to the rail. The PFM ('Power Factor Module') is an isolated, regulated, universal-input AC-DC front end — 'Universal input (85 – 264VAC)', '48V output, regulated, isolated', '400W maximum power', 'Built-in EMI filtering', '127W/in3 power density', 'SELV Output', 'External rectification and transient protection required', 124.75 × 35.54 × 9.40 mm VIA package — with 24 V and 48 V variants. ZVS buck regulators convert a '48V distribution bus directly into multiple secondary voltages – including 12V, 5V, 3.3V, and 2.5V' (Computing page). Neither line is a data-center product at rack scale: the PFM is a 400 W front end and the AC-DC hub lists only 'Converters' and 'Input Modules'.
highlights: The PFM is the only Vicor AC-DC conversion product; there is no Vicor CRPS server supply, power shelf or rectifier shelf — the company's data-center position begins at the DC bus
ZVS bucks are the conventional (non-factorized) end of the point-of-load range for low-current rails
productsAndServices.positioning: Sub-kilowatt, industrial-grade AC-DC and low-current POL — a completeness offer for customers standardizing on Vicor modules, not a contest with the CRPS and shelf vendors (Delta, LITEON, Megmeet, Advanced Energy) at kilowatt scale.
targetSegments: industrial, medical and telecom equipment
defense and test systems

productsAndServices.name: IP licensing practice — patent licences over bus converters, factorized power and vertical power delivery
productsAndServices.description: A second business built on the patent estate ('128 patents having expirations scheduled between 2026 and 2043' in the US at end-2025, per the 10-K). Per the 10-K, 'we seek to license our intellectual property. In granting licenses, we generally retain the right to use our patented technologies and manufacture and sell our products in all licensed geographic areas and fields of use', and 'royalties due to the Company are generally based upon a percentage of the licensee's sales' (Q2 2026 10-Q). Royalty revenue was $15.9M in 2023 (3.9% of net revenues), $46.6M in 2024 (13.0%), $57.4M in 2025 (14.1%) and $45.4M in the first half of 2026 alone ($30.4M in Q2, 21% of the quarter's revenue), on top of a $45.0M patent-litigation settlement received in May 2025. The October 2025 release 'Vicor steps up its IP licensing practice' attributes the expansion to the 2025 ITC Limited Exclusion Order 'that bans importation of infringing bus converters and computing systems', says the resulting settlements and licences represent 'nearly $300 million in expected contribution to Vicor's revenues through 2026', and puts Andrew D'Amico in charge as General Counsel for Intellectual Property. The May 2026 guidance revision announced an OEM's 'all-inclusive license that includes all of Vicor's Patents … including Factorized Power (FPA) and Vertical Power Delivery (VPD)'; on the Q2 2026 call management described that licence as four $5M quarterly payments in its first year and $10M quarterly payments in its second — $60M in total — and said Vicor has 'a multiplicity of OEM licensees, one hyperscaler as of now' (trade-press transcript).
highlights: The lever is the exclusion order, in the CEO's own words: 'Respect for intellectual property is motivated by exclusion orders barring importation of computing systems from infringing suppliers' (May 2026 release); the company 'plans to pursue additional enforcement actions against infringing contract manufacturers and power module makers' (Oct 2025 release)

Licensing revenue exceeded quarterly R&D spending in Q3 2025 (Oct 2025 release); management's stated ambition, per trade-press coverage of the calls, is $200–300M of annual licensing and royalty revenue at 'near-100% gross margin', which is why consolidated gross margin rose from 51.2% (2024) to 58.0% (Q2 2026)

Licensees are not named in any filing or release — the settlement counterparties of May 2025 are 'certain parties' in the 10-K, and the May 2026 licensee is 'an OEM'; the CFO said on the Q2 2026 call that new licences 'may not result until our second ITC case gets to its final determination in 2027' (trade-press transcript)

The practice has a counter-narrative: the ITC found Delta's redesigned products do not infringe two of the three 2023 patents; MPS's Q2 2026 10-Q does not mention Vicor at all; and trade press reports trade-secret suits against Vicor in W.D. Texas in July 2026 by MPS and by Delta, both alleging the patent campaign is a licensing-revenue strategy
productsAndServices.positioning: Unusual among power-module vendors: none of Delta, MPS, Infineon or the shelf vendors runs a licensing business of this weight. Zacks calls it 'a structural advantage that Analog Devices does not share to the same degree'; the risk, stated by Finimize, is that 'Licensing only works if patents stay strong and enforceable' — the 2026 case rests on a single patent issued in August 2025.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct negotiation with OEMs, contract manufacturers and hyperscalers, typically following or under the threat of a Section 337 exclusion order; inquiries routed to Vicor's Intellectual Property Department
targetSegments: AI server OEMs and ODMs (Quanta, Wistron, Wiwynn, Foxconn named as respondents)
hyperscalers buying unlicensed computing systems
power-module makers (Delta, MPS named as respondents)
productsAndServices.roadmap: Record licensing revenue projected for 2026 (Feb 2026 release); the 337-TA-1484 final ID is due May 20, 2027 (target date Sept 20, 2027) and the Federal Circuit appeal of the 2025 Foxconn-licence finding (No. 25-1616) was pending with no decision located as of Sept 3, 2026.

productsAndServices.name: Automotive 48 V power — automotive-grade BCM6135, DCM3735 and PRM3735 for 800 V-to-48 V and 48 V zonal architectures
productsAndServices.description: Introduced in October 2024 as 'new high-density automotive-grade power modules' supporting '800V-to-48V conversion, 48V regulation, and 48V-to-12V regulation': the BCM6135 (800 V nominal, 520–920 V in, 48 V / 32.5–57.5 V out, up to 80 A, 2.5 kW, 97.3% peak, 61 × 35 × 7.4 mm, isolated, bidirectional), the DCM3735 (35–58 V → 8–16 V, 2 kW, up to 160 A, 96.5%) and the PRM3735 (31–58 V → 36–54 V, 2.5 kW, up to 52 A, 99.2%). productsAndServices.name: Aerospace & defense (MIL-COTS, VITA 62/SOSA, radiation-tolerant FPA) and Brick Products for industrial, rail and ATE
productsAndServices.description: MIL-COTS variants of the same module families — BCMs at 'Input: 200–400V, 400–700V, 500–800V | Output: 8.1–55V', 'Up to 125A', 98%; DCMs from 28, 30 and 270 V inputs to 1,300 W; VITA 62 and SOSA-aligned power supplies — 'tested to MIL-STD 704/1275/461/810' per the A&D page, plus radiation-tolerant Factorized Power modules for LEO/MEO satellites presented at JAXA's 38th Microelectronics Workshop (September 2025) and customer stories in adaptive optics (Microgate) and satellite AI (Spacechips). productsAndServices.name: ChiP™ packaging platform and the Andover ChiP fab — panel-level module manufacturing
productsAndServices.category: Manufacturing platform (packaging technology and captive fab)
productsAndServices.description: The manufacturing technology every Advanced Product depends on and the capacity constraint the company now names in every release. ChiP — 'Converter housed in Package' — arrays converters across a printed-circuit panel 'Like wafer fabrication … to utilize 100% of the PCB material', saws the panel into components and plates the exposed 'bar codes' into terminals; package names give the sawn size ('a "4623" package measures 46mm by 23mm'), with two-sided assembly and variants for surface mount (SM-ChiP, 'a plated, overmolded package'), chassis mount (CM-ChiP) and the filtered, PMBus-equipped VIA. Vicor's white paper claims 'a staggering 4X increase in power density and 20% reduction in power loss vs earlier generation components' and 'power densities up to 3kW/in3 … at up to 98% efficiency', with a stated path to '800V and power capability up to 4kW per ChiP-based component'. The panels are built in Andover: a 320,000-square-foot manufacturing building that 'houses all Massachusetts manufacturing activities' (10-K), whose 'world's first ChiP … fabrication facility' opened at 400 Federal Street on May 18, 2022 — a 90,000–95,000 sq ft addition that 'Expanded manufacturing capacity by 2.5x' with pick-and-place at 'up to 420,000 components per hour', in-house electroplating 'previously outsourced to a third-party partner' and 'zero wastewater and air discharge' (company pages and 10-K).
highlights: Capacity is the 2026 story: 'Rising demand … is absorbing increased capacity within our first ChiP fab' (Q1 2026), 'As we get closer to full capacity utilization, we are taking steps toward a second fab for high current density 2nd Gen VPD ChiPs' (Q2 2026); on the Q2 call management said two sites were down-selected for a fab of 'As much as 2x, potentially 3x the first fab' and that Fab 1's revenue capacity had been raised toward $1.5 billion (trade-press transcripts)

Capital-expenditure commitments rose from about $3.9M at end-2025 to about $22.7M at June 30, 2026, 'principally for manufacturing equipment'; capex was $12.4M in Q1 and $11.2M in Q2 2026 versus $4.6M and $6.2M a year earlier (10-Q, releases)
The company earned CHIPS Act advanced-manufacturing investment tax credits on the fab — receivables of $13.2M (2023), $6.3M (2024) and $3.7M (2025) per the 10-K

Single-site risk stated in the 10-K: the fab and all Massachusetts manufacturing are in one owned building, and 'work is underway to bring in-house an additional final step … now conducted by a subcontractor'

The 'alternate source of high current density 2nd Gen VPD modules' Vicor says it is exploring for licensees would be the first time its ChiPs were built elsewhere.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess that Vicor is now two businesses — power modules from one Andover fab and patent licences enforced by exclusion orders — and that the licensing business is the faster-growing and higher-margin of the two. Basis: royalty revenue of $15.9M (3.9% of net revenues) in 2023, $46.6M (13.0%) in 2024, $57.4M (14.1%) in 2025 and $45.4M in the first half of 2026, with Q2 2026 royalty at 21% of revenue on a single new OEM licence structured as $60M over two years; consolidated gross margin rising from 51.2% (2024) to 58.0% (Q2 2026); the company's own October 2025 statement of 'nearly $300 million in expected contribution … through 2026' and its 'record revenues' projection for 2026 licensing (SEC 8-K exhibits, company releases).

(High confidence) We assess that the ITC exclusion order, not the datasheet, is what brought OEMs to the licensing table. Basis: the sequence — final determination February 13, 2025, $45M settlement May 1, 2025, record royalty rate in Q3 2025, all-inclusive OEM licence May 2026 — and the CEO's own words that 'Respect for intellectual property is motivated by exclusion orders barring importation of computing systems from infringing suppliers'; the CFO's statement on the Q2 2026 call that new licences 'may not result until our second ITC case gets to its final determination in 2027' (trade-press transcript) ties the next tranche to the next order.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that Vicor sits outside the NVIDIA 800 VDC ecosystem as published and that its route into those racks is the module socket at the contract manufacturer and the patent over the bus-converter design, not a partner listing. Basis: absence from NVIDIA's May 2025, October 2025 and March 2026 partner lists while Delta, LITEON, Megmeet, MPS, Infineon and TI are named; SemiAnalysis's independent account of Vicor's design-out from H100 in favour of MPS; and the 2026 ITC respondents — Quanta, Wistron, Wiwynn, Luxshare, Delta, MPS — being exactly the ODMs and vendors that build the racks. The counter-evidence is Vicor's 2026 backlog (+145% YoY) and management's claim of one hyperscaler licensee.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that the second-generation vertical-power-delivery ramp is the product thesis and is unproven in the field. Basis: Vicor's only first-party references to '5th generation ChiPs and 2nd Generation VPD' are CEO sentences in results releases — no datasheet, part number or package exists on its site; the lead customer is unnamed (trade press infers Cerebras, which the CEO declined to confirm); Craig-Hallum's independent caveat that the product 'lacks field experience'; and the 10-K's one-customer concentration of 11.1% of 2025 revenues with Advanced Products customers 'concentrated in the data center and hyperscaler segments'. A Q1 2026 production launch was stated on the Q3 2025 call; volume ramps were placed in late 2027 on the Q2 2026 call.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that manufacturing capacity is the binding constraint on product revenue through 2027 and the largest single-site risk in the file's power-module set. Basis: 'Rising demand … is absorbing increased capacity within our first ChiP fab' and 'As we get closer to full capacity utilization, we are taking steps toward a second fab' (Q1 and Q2 2026 releases); capital-expenditure commitments rising from $3.9M at end-2025 to $22.7M at June 30, 2026; two sites down-selected with a decision 'in the coming weeks' as of July 21 and none announced by September 3; and the 10-K's statement that one owned Andover building 'houses all Massachusetts manufacturing activities'. The stated exploration of an 'alternate source' for VPD modules would be the first ChiPs built outside Andover.

(Low confidence) We assess that the second litigation campaign carries more legal risk than the first and that licensing revenue beyond 2026 depends on its outcome. Basis: 337-TA-1484 rests on one patent issued August 19, 2025; the first case's own findings included redesigned Delta products that do not infringe and a purchase-order licence for Foxconn's FII USA and Ingrasys that Vicor is still appealing (CAFC 25-1616, no decision located); MPS's 10-Q does not mention Vicor; and trade press reports trade-secret counter-suits by MPS and Delta in July 2026. The judgment is low-confidence because the ITC record, the CAFC docket and the counter-suits could be read only in part through this session's proxy.

(Moderate confidence) We assess key-person and governance concentration as a material risk the company does not address. Basis: a founder who is chairman, president and CEO at 79, controls ten-vote Class B shares, and whose 2026 proxy contains no succession language; an eleven-member board unchanged from 2025; both the product architecture and the litigation strategy are his in the company's own telling (2019 IEEE Newell award, 'more than 100 patents').

Collection gap: Vicor's investor site was unreachable throughout (HTTP 403/503), so results were read from its SEC 8-K exhibits and one GlobeNewswire copy; no licensee, settlement counterparty or lead VPD customer is named in any primary source; the USITC's own documents for the 2026 investigation were blocked and its schedule is known from a search snippet and the CFO's call remark; Nasdaq and Zacks consensus pages could not be captured, so 'expected' figures are aggregator-tracker values with both shown where they disagree; the July 2026 trade-secret suits are known from a Law360 lede and a newspaper snippet and were not verified against the complaints.

INDICATORS TO WATCH — *~20 Oct 2026 — Q3 2026 results (tracker-estimated, not company-confirmed; Vicor announces its call about two weeks ahead):* royalty revenue against Q2's $30.4M would confirm or refute Judgment 1's run-rate ($5M was guided from the newest licence for Q3 versus $15M in Q2); product revenue against the $380M backlog would test Judgment 5's capacity ceiling. *Any date — second-fab site announcement:* confirms Judgment 5; a further delay past year-end would indicate the capital plan is slipping. *2026–27 — 337-TA-1484 milestones (Markman, evidentiary hearing, final ID due 20 May 2027, target date 20 Sept 2027):* a violation finding would confirm Judgment 2's mechanism; a no-violation or licence finding would confirm Judgment 6. *Any date — Federal Circuit decision in No. 25-1616:* reversal of the Foxconn licence finding would widen the first order's reach. *Q1 2027 — sampling of improved 2nd-gen VPD (per trade press, to Cerebras):* a named customer or a datasheet would move Judgment 4 to moderate-high. *Next NVIDIA 800 VDC partner list (GTC 2027):* Vicor's appearance would refute Judgment 3. *W.D. Texas — MPS and Delta trade-secret suits:* a preliminary-injunction ruling either way would change the licensing calculus.

Texas case against Delta May 13, 2025, within two weeks of the $45M settlement whose counterparties Vicor does not name.

Texas (stayed February 24, 2026 pending the ITC) and the 337-TA-1484 investigation with Delta and DET Logistics among fifteen respondents, on a target date of September 20, 2027. summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Vicor is the point-of-load and bus-converter silicon vendor for the 48 V and 800 V AI rack whose revenue has been re-based by patent enforcement — a February 2025 ITC exclusion order over its bus-converter patents turned royalties from 3.9% of revenue in 2023 into 21% of the June 2026 quarter, while its single Andover ChiP fab approaches capacity on a second-generation vertical-power-delivery ramp for a lead customer it will not name; the next verifiable tests are the Q3 2026 results expected around 20 October 2026 (unconfirmed), the second-fab site decision management said in July was weeks away, and the May 2027 initial determination in its second ITC case against Delta, Monolithic Power Systems and the server ODMs. BACKGROUND. Founded in Andover, Massachusetts in 1981 by Patrizio Vinciarelli, who remains chairman, president and CEO at 79 with ten-vote Class B shares; NASDAQ: VICR; 1,092 full-time employees at end-2025 per the 10-K; one reportable segment split between Advanced Products (the Factorized Power Architecture — PRM regulators, VTM current multipliers, Power-on-Package and vertical power delivery — plus BCM, NBM and DCM converters) and legacy Brick Products (39.0% of 2025 net revenues). FY2025 revenue was $452.7M including a $45.0M patent-litigation settlement (net revenues $407.7M: product $350.3M, royalty $57.4M), net income $118.6M; Q2 2026 revenue $143.4M with royalty $30.4M, backlog $380M and cash $453.6M, per SEC 8-K exhibits. Products are built on a proprietary panel-level 'ChiP' process in one company-owned 320,000-square-foot Andover building whose fab opened in May 2022; the company earned CHIPS Act advanced-manufacturing credits on it. The IP practice, headed by a General Counsel for Intellectual Property since October 2025, rests on 128 US patents; the ITC found a Section 337 violation on two of three patents in February 2025 (with Delta's redesigned products non-infringing and Foxconn affiliates licensed), a $45M settlement with unnamed parties followed in May 2025, an all-inclusive OEM licence structured as $60M over two years followed in May 2026, and a second investigation on a patent issued in August 2025 was instituted in February 2026 with a target date of September 2027. Vicor is absent from every NVIDIA 800 VDC partner list published since May 2025.
ecosystemRole: We assess Vicor as this corpus's reference for the last centimetre of the AI power chain — the fixed-ratio bus converters that take an 800 V or 400 V rack bus to 48 V, and the current multipliers that take 48 V to about one volt at a thousand amps beside or beneath the processor — and the one vendor in the file paid for that idea twice, as a module built in its own fab and as a licence enforced at the border. Basis: its 10-K's description of the Factorized Power Architecture and Power-on-Package, its datasheets, and the ITC's 2025 determination. Against the shelf vendors this app covers (Delta, LITEON, Megmeet), Vicor sells the converter component rather than the shelf, and against the multiphase-regulator vendors on NVIDIA's 800 VDC silicon lists it sells an architecture rather than a part; it is the natural anchor for how a DC bus is stepped down inside the rack and, because a BBU or supercapacitor shelf lives on the same bus, for where a storage seller's in-rack conversation begins.
